one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window. (1) Q3 2026 earnings, estimated for Monday Oct 26 after the close. The date is not yet confirmed by the company: Investing.com and MarketChameleon estimate it from last year's timing, and the Q2 webcast was announced three weeks ahead. Q3 guidance is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 non-GAAP EPS against an $8.1B backlog. Cadence normally beats and raises, but the reaction base rate is not bullish: a 41% positive one-day rate over 17 prints, with a median up move of +7% and a median down move of -2% (Trefis). The July 27 raise gave +1.8% on Jul 28 and then -3.5% on Jul 29 (Twelve Data daily). (2) The FOMC on Oct 28. Polymarket has 74% no change and 26% a 25bp hike, on $21.3M volume. The 10-year Treasury is at 5.29% (Fed H.15, Sep 30), and higher yields were the stated driver of the early-September software sell-off. Short-horizon setup: the stock has rallied 28% in 12 sessions, from $273.96 (Sep 15) to $350.75. The drivers were the ChipStack RTL agent (Sep 22), TSMC A14 certification (Sep 24) and SNPS +9-13% after its Sep 30 investor day. In CDNS's own history, the month after a gain of more than 12% has a median return of about 0% (n=20, SD about 7%). So there is no momentum edge and no reliable reversal edge either. I centre at about $351.5 (spot plus a hair for the usual beat-and-raise) with a monthly sigma of about 12.5% (41%/3.5 plus an earnings and FOMC bump), roughly lognormal.

fair_value.method: Blended 12-month-forward value of $348 (was $374). Weights: 50% P/E (blended NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $10.65 x 34x = $362), 30% FCF yield (NTM FCF/share at Oct-2027 of about $8.70 at a 2.4% yield = $362) and 20% DCF (FCF $1.84B growing 18% for 5 years and then 12%, WACC 10% on a 5.29% 10-year yield, terminal growth 4% = $266 today, rolled forward to $293).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Blended NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $10.65 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $9.56 + 0.75 x FY28 estimate ~$11.0) x 34x

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus across 26 analysts, which replaces the old $9.54-9.76 range taken from an aggregator.

FY27 consensus of $9.56 grown about 15%. That matches FY26's 14% EPS growth and Synopsys's new mid-teens EPS CAGR framework to FY2030 for the same end-market. Cadence management also flagged possible 2027 margin improvement after the Hexagon integration.
0.25 x 9.56 + 0.75 x 11.0. This corrects round 1, which used the FY28 figure of $11.0 itself as the blended NTM.

CDNS is at 38.5x forward today (StockAnalysis). The 10-year TTM P/E range is about 16-101x (GuruFocus). SNPS is at about 25x FY27 EPS ($475.70 / $19.08 guide) after its investor day re-rating. The 10-year Treasury at 5.29% (H.15) is about 1 point higher than I assumed in round 1, which argues for more compression than the 36x I used then. I keep a premium to SNPS for hardware and IP momentum.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF/share at Oct-2027 of about $8.70 / 2.4% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 FCF of about $1.84B (OCF $2.0B less about $0.16B capex) / 276.5M shares = $6.65. Grown about 17% gives FY27 $7.80 and FY28 about $9.0, blended 0.25/0.75 to $8.70. The growth is cross-checked against Synopsys's guide of mid-20s FCF CAGR to FY30, which I deliberately fade.
The current P/FCF of 56x is a 1.8% yield. I de-rate it to about 42x, consistent with the P/E method and a 5.29% risk-free rate.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF0 $1.84B; growth 18% for years 1-5 and 12% for years 6-10; terminal growth 4%; WACC 10%; net debt $1.12B; 276.5M shares. Value today of $266, rolled forward 12 months at 10% = $293.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 revenue growth guide of 19%, record $8.1B backlog, and management's possible 2027 margin improvement. Synopsys guides mid-20s FCF CAGR to FY30. I set this slightly below revenue growth plus margin.

Risk-free 5.29% (10-year, H.15, Sep 30, 2026) + beta 1.14 x ERP of about 4.3%, giving about 10.2%, rounded to 10%. Leverage is negligible. Round 1 used a 4.3% risk-free rate, which the H.15 data now contradicts.
EDA is a secular grower: Synopsys targets 13%+ EDA CAGR to FY2030. I fade that toward nominal GDP plus.

bear.story: Multiple compresses to about 23-24x NTM EPS of about $10.4, i.e. SNPS parity. Possible triggers: rates keep climbing (10-year already 5.29%, a Fed hike still priced at 26% for October); the AI-disruption narrative returns (Kimi K3 open-source chip demo, -9.5% on Jul 17, 2026; AI-native EDA start-ups); or China friction after the trade truce lapses on Jan 10, 2027 (2025 BIS EDA ban precedent). A 2027 recession (Kalshi about 20%, Polymarket 35% on thin volume) would add to this. Ends near the 2026 lows ($262.75) or below.

base.story: 15-19% revenue growth, FY27 EPS near the $9.56 consensus and blended NTM EPS of about $10.65 at a roughly 34x multiple. EPS growth is partly eaten by further de-rating, like the past year (price -0.2% while EPS grew about 14%).

bull.story: Agentic AI (ChipStack, ViraStack; consumption revenue excluded from guidance) and record hardware demand lift FY27-28 estimates to about $11.4 NTM, and the 2025-26 peak multiple of about 42x returns. Sector support from SNPS's raised FY27 guide and long-term framework, plus yields easing from multi-decade highs. Retests and breaks the $416.69 52-week high.

thesis_break_reason: About $245 is about 7% below the 52-week low of $262.75 and about 23x NTM EPS, below SNPS's 25x. Even after the AI-disruption scare (Jul 17) and the September rate and software sell-off, the stock held about $274. Trading at $245 would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than 41%-vol noise: a guidance cut or bookings slowdown, renewed China EDA export restrictions after the truce, or evidence that AI agents are actually eroding EDA seat pricing. The 2025 trough of about $221 needed the April 2025 tariff shock plus the BIS EDA ban.

reasoning: Base rates. CDNS month-end closes 2006-2026 (Twelve Data): forward 12-month log returns have a median of +20%, SD 0.36, P(drop more than 25%) 8% and P(gain more than 35%) 33%. Starts in the last 10 years: median +27%, SD 0.20. The 41 starts after a flat trailing year had a +24% median. These numbers are inflated by a 15-year re-rating, and the regime has clearly shifted: the price is about +13% a year over 3 years with EPS growing about 15%, and it was flat over the past year while EPS grew about 14%. So I discount the historical drift heavily. Monthly-close vol is about 29-31%, below the 41% daily realized vol, which is elevated by 2026's event-driven swings. Event odds, verified this round: Kalshi's next-year (2027) recession odds hit an all-time low of 20% on Sep 26 (Kalshi post; Oddsshopper had the 2027 contract at 38-39c on Aug 4 with about 88K contracts traded). That is lower than the thin $9.6K Polymarket market at 35%, so I trimmed the macro left tail. Rates moved the other way: the 10-year is 5.29% and the 2-year 4.88% (H.15), and Polymarket gives 26% to an October hike ($21.3M volume). That raised my WACC to 10% and cut the DCF from $343 to $293. Policy: the Sep 25-27 Xi-Trump summit extended the truce only to Jan 10, 2027, with no chip export-control relief (Fortune). Polymarket gives a 13% chance of a China invasion of Taiwan by end-2027 ($3.3M volume), a fat-tail risk for the whole semi complex. A new bear thread I had not chased: the Jul 17, 2026 Kimi K3 open-source chip demo knocked CDNS down 9.5%. The SemiWiki forum and BNP are sceptical (the demo was at 45nm), but a cluster of AI-native EDA start-ups is real. Bull side: SNPS's FY27 guide (+15% revenue, $19.04-19.12 EPS, mid-teens to FY30, 13%+ EDA CAGR) supports the sector, and Cadence keeps agentic consumption revenue out of guidance. Fundamentals: FY26 guide $6.26-6.34B revenue and $8.05-8.15 EPS, consensus FY27 $9.56, average target $405 (26 analysts). Correcting my NTM EPS ($10.65, not $11.0) and the higher discount rate bring fair value to $348, about spot. Scenarios of $250/$365/$480 at 25/50/25 give an EV of about $365. Ladder: a lognormal with median $360 (+2.6%, between fair value and modest EPS-driven drift; the sell-side target of $405 is evidence, not the anchor) and sigma 0.37, with slightly fattened tails.
